newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: ZIMBABWE DOLLAR CLOSES FIRMER ON UNITS.
newsitem.headline: ZIMBABWE DOLLAR CLOSES FIRMER ON UNITS.

text.p: The Zimbabwe dollar closed firmer against hard currencies on Tuesday, pushed up by the central bank which came into the market with U.S. dollars, dealers said.
"The Reserve Bank dumped a few dollars into the market," one dealer said.
"I'm not quite sure why because there were no big payments made today...The market was pretty quiet with very little trading."
Traders said it appeared the bank was trying to smoothe any fears of a slide in the Zimbabwe dollar.
"I think the message they are trying to put across is that, 'don't panic, the money is there if you need it.'"
The local unit finished the day at 10.5900/6100 against the U.S. dollar, up from Monday's 10.6000/6200.

Against the crosses, it was also quoted firmer on sterling at 17.0220/0650 compared to 17.0900/1500 but slipped against the German mark to 7.0090/0270 from 6.9600/9800, tracking a softer U.S. dollar overseas.
It edged up against the ailing South African rand to 2.2570/2640 from the previous day's 2.2800/2900. --Stella Mapenzauswa, Harare Newsroom: +263-4 72 52 27/8/9--
